items.statement: Working capital requirements are met from internal accruals and commission show accruals; the flywheel sustains itself.
items.quote: The working capital requirements don't change that much, simply because, as I said, it's a business of fixed investment and just incrementals as they keep coming in. So the working capital is able to take care of from internal accruals.

items.statement: Other current assets of INR80 crores include project advances, content creation, receivables of INR14-15 crores, and inventory of INR21 crores for an uncommercialized project.
items.quote: Yes, so this is including some advances for this project, which we are in the pipeline for a subsidiary and content creations majorly, and which also include receivable around INR14 crores, INR15 crores. Plus there will be an inventory of INR21 crores, which is in a project which is developed yet not commercialized for revenue.

items.statement: Working capital cycle increased from 68 days to 97 days due to extra credit given to select exporters
items.quote: This year as of September, we have given additional credit to few select exporters. 12:33 So it has gone up by 20-30 days

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected to return to 68 days once Trump tariff situation improves
items.quote: We expect to bring that back to 68 days, which is currently at 97 days.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents declined from Rs. 3.26 crores to Rs. 1.59 crores due to CAPEX and working capital requirements
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents have declined from Rs. 3.26 crores to 1.59 due to CAPEX and working capital requirements.

items.statement: Working capital remains very healthy
items.quote: Our working capital remains very healthy.

items.statement: No plan to increase stake in Bootes Infra; remains at 51% Univastu, 49% Bootes
items.quote: No, no, there is no plan to increase the stake in Bootes Infra. We, started with the 51-49, 51% is the Univastu, and 49% is the Bootes Infra.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increased due to front-loading of expenses; utilization to normalize to 80-85% of limits in coming quarters
items.quote: the borrowings will reduce in the sense they will come in line in the proportion in which we have, generally been utilizing the funds, about 80% to 85% of the total facilities.

items.statement: May go for equity raise instead of debt if major order received
items.quote: If we got a major order, we will surely go for the equity instead of debt.

items.statement: Management says debtor days have improved and no payment has turned into bad debt; receivables are managed actively with government and cooperative bank clients.
items.quote: So, you find that the debtor day ratio has improved as well. So, our team is continuously discussing with the client. We try to focus all the problems which they have. So, getting the payment is never the problem for us. And not a single payment has been retained or kept by the bank or goes into the bad debt.

items.statement: Management explains INR 23 crore long-term loans and advances is an advance paid to a vendor for data center expansion, to be reclassified to plant and machinery in H2 FY26.
items.quote: Yes, sir. So, also if the loan which has been sanctioned from the bank is shown under the loans and liabilities, and this is the advance given to the party, vendor, who is supplying the data center to us.

items.statement: Board voluntarily adopted quarterly financial reporting despite SME requirement being half-yearly, and approved a dividend distribution policy plus a 10% interim dividend.
items.quote: Although SME listed entities are required to report only half yearly, this is a forward-looking measure that aligns us with the transparent governance practices. The board also adopted a dividend distribution policy, reinforcing our principles of disciplined capital allocation and equitable shareholders' rewards. And as further declared a 10% interim dividend i.e. Rs 1 per equity share of face val

items.statement: Management acknowledges investor suggestion to engage a larger auditor for credibility and says they are bringing more transparency through voluntary quarterly reporting.
items.quote: Sir, there is one more explanation for it. That is why we have adopted voluntarily the quarterly reporting to bring more transparency and confidence within you.

items.statement: Operating cash flow has not grown in line with profitability due to prolonged working capital cycles and longer project cycles, especially during monsoon season.
items.quote: So, definitely, the project cycle is long, and duri ng the monsoon season the project cycle becomes even longer. As projects are getting larger, it definitely takes more time to collect

items.statement: CEO Ramanuj Mukherjee and co-founder Abhyuday each bought shares worth ₹12 lakh and ₹10 lakh respectively in the last six months and plan similar purchases in the next six months.
items.quote: I bought ₹12 Lakhs of shares in the last 6 months, and Abhyuday bought ₹10 Lakhs. We plan to do similar buying in the next 6 months.

items.statement: A tech co-founder resigned due to approaching retirement age (close to 60), achieving financial goals, and finding the role stressful.
items.quote: One tech co-founder resigned. He was approaching retirement age (close to 60) and achieved his financial goals. He found it stressful and wanted to retire.

items.statement: Management confirms sufficient cash in bank; major spending on AI and university setup is mostly done and future approach will be more conservative.
items.quote: Yes, we have enough money. Going forward, we will be more conservative. The major spending on AI and the University setup is mostly done.

items.statement: No fundraise planned because stock price is too low; aim to improve cash position from internal cash flow.
items.quote: No. Our stock price is too low to raise funds. We aim to improve our cash position from our own cash flow.

items.statement: No cash crunch; inventory and receivables rose with sales but banking limits unchanged and free limits available
items.quote: No, so there is no cash crunch that we are seeing. In fact, just to apprise you that, this year we have not even taken any additional banking limits, that we have been, you know, year on year, that is, incremental limits we have been always taking, but this year we have not taken the same.

items.statement: Debtor days reduced from 60 to 48 as of October 2025 through credit control norms
items.quote: implementation of c redit control norms , and that also helps us in cash flow management, and reducing our debtor days from 60 to 48. As of October 2025

items.statement: Inventory controls tightened across depots and factory improving working capital and cash flow management
items.quote: As an inventory management initiative, yes, we de finitely tightened our inventory controls, and now, you know, we are basically controlling our inventories across depots, as well as in the factory premises also, on very strict norms

items.statement: Debtor insurance obtained to support new customer relationships and top-line growth
items.quote: So, to mitigate risks, what we have done this time is that we have gone ahead and obtained a debtor insurance. This will help us be more confident in approaching customers and starting new relationships, which I think will continue to reflect in the top line.

items.statement: Working capital cycle deteriorating due to sales shift to large pharma customers with 90-day payment terms
items.quote: The debtor days in most of the pharma space is 90 days. So, we are seeing an increase in our debtors, specifically on the working capital front.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations expected to remain negative for a while as sales momentum increases
items.quote: So, we expect the cash flows from operations to be negative for a while as we continue to increase the sales momentum, this will start plateauing once all our facilities are on.

items.statement: Plan to use bill discounting aggressively with AAA-rated large customers to manage working capital
items.quote: Our plan is to use bill discounting aggressively as we move into the top tier customer base, those facilities are available to us and we think we will be able to manage with that.

items.statement: No current plan to raise capital but will not shy away if required
items.quote: So capital, as if not, there has been no plan, but if it is required, we'll definitely won't shy to take any decision.

items.statement: Auditor found inventory valued higher by Rs 2.86 crore and depreciation discrepancy of Rs 27.47 lakh; corrected in FY25.
items.quote: the current auditor found that difference, and that's why we actually corrected in the year FY 24-25. so that is the difference that you see of Rs 2.86 crore where you know it was valued at a higher side, and he wanted to correct that at some point of time, because it was needed also, and that is what has been mentioned in the management report as well.

items.statement: Inventory turnover 232 days, receivables turnover 104 days, payables 55 days for H1 FY26.

items.statement: Inventory composition: WIP 40-45%, raw material <30%, finished goods 20-25%, consumables balance.

items.statement: Raw material stock built up to lock prices after tungsten prices rose over 100%.
items.quote: the price of tungsten end of March and end of today is more than 100% now we don't want to make a significant loss. So for that reason, also, we have actually procured raw material and blocked that price so that we don't make a loss in processing.

But overall, the you know cash flow should be positive maybe from the second-half of next year.

items.quote: Total income for this Q2 was at INR 149.5 crores, and EBITDA margin was INR 13.7 crores, whereas PAT margin was minus 28% due to the exceptional item.

items.quote: we are taking necessary corrective action, and hopefully we'll… you'll see the outcome when we, declare our results i n the, in the next, for the H2

items.quote: So, these are typically the advances and that we would have given to our agents to help them grow their business.

items.quote: These are not outstanding unreceivable. These are tyres physically available in these places for marketing to the customers.

items.quote: Our receivable outstanding for over 6 months overall, where 19 crores last year.

items.quote: Please note that the Company has INR 2,449 million, that is about INR 245 crore of bank balances, other than the cash and cash equivalents, which is kept as fixed deposits in the bank.

items.quote: But when we come to the net cash from operating activities, that has decreased from INR 24 crores previous year to INR 6 crores this year.

items.quote: Based upon valuation, the merger proposal suggests that for every 08 shares of CMRSL, investors of CMRSL will get 35 shares of CMIL.

items.statement: Merger expected to improve cash flow and enable efficient capital utilization
items.quote: The merger will also improve cash flow resulting in efficient utilization of capital.

items.quote: As all of you may know that the Board of Directors has recommended the merger of CMRSL with Cyber Media (India) Limited (CMIL). In fact, this was also a recommendation that was raised in the previous calls by the investors.

items.quote: We had a positive response to the rights issue from CMIL's shareholders. It was subscribed as 82.38%.

items.quote: As per CMIL's balance sheet, there are immovable assets, i.e. land and building which have a fair market value under advisement of approx. INR 27 crore.

items.statement: Merger expected to complete in 6-9 months subject to regulatory approvals, likely next financial year
items.quote: The merger is likely to take approx. six to nine months ' time, subject to approvals from relevant authorities involved. It is expected that the merger will complete in the next financial year.

items.statement: Management expects annual cost savings of at least INR 1 crore in merged entity from reduced compliance and better tax planning
items.quote: The management expects a cost saving of at least INR 1 crore annually in a merged entity.

items.statement: Total merger cost estimated between INR 40-50 lakh, expected to be recovered within six months through cost savings
items.quote: The total merger cost is estimated between INR 40 Lakh to INR 50 Lakh. But in case, we look at the cost-saving part, as Mr. Dhaval Gupta has mentioned, cost saving will be at least INR 1 crore per year. So, the merger cost is going to repay itself within the first six months.

items.quote: On a Rs. 100 crores-Rs. 120 crores revenue, I think we are expecting 30% plus EBITDA from this plant. Our initial estimate is this, this should be in 'FY26-'27, first year of operation.

items.statement: Working capital requirement for job work is limited to colours and chemicals; core raw material supplied by customer.
items.quote: Because we are doing job work, working capital requirement is limited. Our raw material investment is mainly colours and chemicals; the core raw material is supplied by the customer.

items.quote: For around ₹200 crore turnover, which we are targeting from FY26–27, we may take a banking facility of around ₹20–₹30 crore, if required. That is available because currently there is zero bank debt.

items.quote: While profitability was lower compared to the same period last year, it is important to highlight that the company remained profitable and operationally stable, despite the challenging environment.

items.quote: Last week, we had announced that Protean Board had approved the acquisition o f 4.95% equity stake in NS DL Payments Bank Limited for approximately a value of INR 30.2 crores

items.quote: Basically, if you see your financial year 2025, we had a receivable of 36 days, which has now reduced to 33 days. So we are working on reducing our working capital cycle.
